# Proverbs 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** My child, if you truly take in what I'm saying and hold my instructions close to your heart,

**2** If you tune your ears to wisdom and open your mind to understanding,

**3** If you actually cry out for insight and beg for understanding,

**4** If you go after it the way you'd hunt for silver — digging for it like buried treasure —

**5** Then you will grasp what it means to honor the LORD, and you will discover who God really is.

**6** Because the LORD Himself is the source of wisdom; knowledge and understanding come straight from Him.

**7** He has stored up success for those who live with integrity; He stands as a shield over those who walk honestly,

**8** Protecting those who pursue justice and watching over those who are faithful to Him.

**9** Then you will understand what it means to do right — fairness, justice, every path that leads somewhere good.

**10** Because wisdom will settle into your heart, and knowledge will become something your soul genuinely enjoys.

**11** Good judgment will stand guard over you, and understanding will keep you safe,

**12** Rescuing you from people who are heading the wrong way — from those whose words twist the truth,

**13** People who have left behind the honest road to walk down dark paths,

**14** Who actually enjoy doing harm and celebrate when things go wrong,

**15** Whose lives are full of detours and whose ways are crooked through and through.

**16** Wisdom will also protect you from the seductive outsider — the smooth-talking woman who leads you astray,

**17** Who abandoned the partner she married young and forgot the sacred promises she made before God.

**18** Her house is a dead end — literally. Her path leads to the world of the dead.

**19** No one who goes to her finds their way back; they never return to the land of the living.

**20** So walk with good people. Stay on the road that honest men and women travel.

**21** Because those who live with integrity will enjoy the land, and people of honesty will remain secure in it,

**22** But those who do wrong will lose everything, and the dishonest will be torn out by the roots.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **2:1-4**: The metaphor of treasure-hunting is brilliant — it says wisdom won't just fall in your lap. You have to want it badly enough to dig.

- **2:17**: The 'covenant of her God' likely refers to the marriage covenant. The idea that marriage has a divine witness is important here.

— PNEUMA
